title: SDK integration walkthrough (Python/TypeScript) - BrightHealth Analytics

Agreed next steps: share quickstart repos, security docs, and schedule a POC benchmark next week.

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-08
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~46 minutes
Attendees: Alex Rivera (AE), Priya Nair (SE) - Redwood Inference; Jordan Lee (CTO), Maya Ortiz (Backend Engineer), Samir Patel (DevOps), Leah Kim (Security) - BrightHealth Analytics

[00:00] Alex Rivera: hey everyone thanks for joining, um we wanted to focus today on the SDK integration walkthrough, python and typescript, auth patterns and a quick demo of the console snippets, and we'll leave time for questions. you good with that, Jordan?
[00:08] Jordan Lee: yeah that sounds great, thanks Alex. we're mainly interested in how fast we can get a prototype up and running and what the auth story looks like for our internal services.
[00:15] Alex Rivera: perfect. quick intro - i'm alex i'm the account exec. priya is our solutions engineer, she'll run the code demos and answer infra/perf questions.
[00:23] Priya Nair: hi all, hey. i'll do the live quickstarts, show env var setup, token rotation patterns and a short benchmark script we use for initial POCs.
[00:30] Maya Ortiz: great. for context, our stack is node/back end services in k8s, some python data processing pipelines, and we have strict security controls - we use a KMS and require audit logs.
[00:38] Samir Patel: also we deploy in multiple regions and care a lot about latency for interactive features.
[00:43] Alex Rivera: thanks. we'll show both hosted and the dedicated/private paths and touch on what to expect for latency vs cost.

[02:05] Priya Nair: starting with Python quickstart - i'll paste into chat the repo link, but basically pip install redwood-inference-sdk (note: this package name is illustrative in the demo). sample code:
- set REDWOOD_API_KEY as an env var or use the secrets manager pattern
- from redwood import Client; client = Client(api_key=os.getenv('REDWOOD_API_KEY'))
- resp = client.generate(prompt='summarize the clinical note')
This pattern works out of the box for hosted api.

[03:12] Jordan Lee: small question, do you support OIDC or service-to-service tokens for rotation?
[03:18] Priya Nair: yes, you can use API keys stored in your KMS, we support KMS integrations and you can rotate keys regularly. we also support short-lived tokens via our OIDC flow for private deployments; for hosted we use scoped API keys. there was a small typo in our docs earlier that said OIDC was beta but it's GA now.

[04:10] Alex Rivera: note on envs - for k8s we recommend storing the REDWOOD_API_KEY in your cluster secrets or using workload identity to fetch short-lived creds.

[05:00] Priya Nair: switching to TypeScript quickstart - npm install @redwood/inference (demo name) then:
- import { Client } from '@redwood/inference';
- const client = new Client({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY });
- const res = await client.chat.create({ messages: [...] });
we also show streaming in the SDK so you can incrementally render tokens in the browser.

[06:20] Maya Ortiz: streaming looks useful. how does that work with our front end - do you proxy through our servers or call the hosted endpoint directly from the client?
[06:30] Priya Nair: recommended pattern is proxying through your backend for auth + observability. we have a lightweight websocket example in the quickstart. if you call directly, ensure tokens are short-lived and scoped.

[07:40] Samir Patel: what's the recommended batching strategy? our throughput bursts a lot during business hours.
[07:48] Priya Nair: good question - our SDK exposes an async batcher. for real time interactive use keep batch sizes small (1-4) and concurrency higher; for background processing use larger batches. in the Optimize tab of the console we can suggest batching and quantization profiles based on sample traffic.

[09:55] Alex Rivera: i'll share a benchmark script that uses the SDK's batcher. it simulates concurrent clients and records p95/p99 latencies.

[12:15] Priya Nair: demoing the Console - here's how you create an API key, set usage quotas, and view per-route token costs. (background typing sounds) the console also surfaces Optimize recommendations - e.g., try 4-bit quantized variant for embedding-heavy jobs to cut cost by ~40% while keeping quality.

[14:02] Leah Kim: on security we need SOC2 artifacts, audit logs, and an assurance that logs do not include PII. are audit logs available per-tenant?
[14:12] Alex Rivera: yes, we provide audit logs and you can configure retention. for private deployments audit logs remain in your VPC; for hosted we provide redaction controls and optional enterprise retention settings. we'll send the SOC2 and data handling FAQ after the call.

[16:40] Jordan Lee: what about private deployments? we might need a VPC or on-prem option for certain datasets.

[16:50] Priya Nair: for Private we offer a customer-controlled control plane with optional on-prem bundle. networking can be VPC-peered or on-prem air-gapped. we integrate with your KMS/HSM for key management. performance parity is good but you'll want dedicated GPU nodes to hit low single-digit token latencies.

[19:05] Maya Ortiz: any gotchas for our k8s infra? we use Istio and have strict egress rules.
[19:13] Priya Nair: you'll just need to allow egress to our control plane endpoints if using hosted; private deployments avoid that. we have examples for sidecar configs and sample network policies in the quickstart. sometimes Istio mTLS settings require tweaks for streaming websockets - we have a KB on that.

[21:30] Alex Rivera: cost question - how do you recommend we think about hosted vs dedicated?
[21:38] Priya Nair: hosted is fastest to start, pay-as-you-go. Dedicated reserved capacity buys predictable throughput and lower unit cost for high volume. Optimize helps you choose quantization and batching to hit cost targets. we can model expected spend once you share sample traffic.

[24:00] Samir Patel: do you have rate limits or quotas per api key? we have internal burst behaviour.

[24:08] Alex Rivera: yes, by default there are per-key rate limits but they can be adjusted for Dedicated customers. we also support client-side rate limiting in the SDK.

[26:45] Priya Nair: quick note on telemetry - the SDK emits minimal traces for latency and token usage. console shows token breakdown by route and model. you can forward logs to your SIEM.

[28:10] Jordan Lee: we'd like to validate quality regressions. what's your eval workflow?

[28:20] Priya Nair: we have an evals integration where you can attach prompt sets and measure delta between model versions; Optimize can alert on regressions. for POC we'll help set up a small eval harness.

[30:40] Maya Ortiz: can we run the POC in eu-west region? data residency is a must for some subsets.

[30:48] Alex Rivera: yes, we have region options for hosted and Dedicated; Private gives full control. we'll note your preference for eu-west for the POC.

[32:00] Priya Nair: showing the benchmark script now - it hits the client.generate endpoint, varies batch sizes, and records p50/p95/p99. example output: p95 ~ 220ms for small prompts on a dedicated variant in our demo infra. actual numbers vary by model, seq len and infra.

[34:15] Samir Patel: what models do you recommend for short clinical summarization vs embeddings?

[34:24] Priya Nair: for summaries a mid-sized LLM with instruction tuning is good; for embeddings we have specialized embedding models. Optimize will recommend model and quantization for your workload. also if you need strict latency use lower-latency variants or pin to dedicated nodes.

[36:40] Leah Kim: KMS: does Redwood manage keys in hosted or do we bring our own?

[36:48] Alex Rivera: both: hosted supports Redwood-managed keys by default and BYOK via popular KMS providers for enterprise tiers; private deployments integrate with your KMS/HSM. we'll share the KMS integration doc.

[38:55] Jordan Lee: ok so next steps - we want the quickstarts and a benchmark script. we'll provide payloads and target RPS. also need the security pack.

[39:10] Alex Rivera: confirmed. i'll send the Python and TS quickstart repos, the console demo recording, and the security FAQ. priya will send the benchmark script.

[40:40] Priya Nair: small caveat - sometimes transcripts in our docs show product names wrong (redwood inform etc) - sorry about that, docs team is cleaning them up.

[41:00] Maya Ortiz: (laughs) noted. one more question: do you support model rollouts A/B?

[41:10] Priya Nair: yes, rollouts are in Console - canary, A/B, automatic fallback to a cheaper variant on errors. good for safe model upgrades.

[42:30] Samir Patel: if we want to replicate this in our staging, how long to spin up a dedicated node for test?

[42:40] Alex Rivera: for a POC we can reserve a small dedicated pool within a few days; hosted is instant. we'll coordinate timing during POC kickoff.

[44:05] Jordan Lee: sounds good. thanks everyone.

[44:12] Alex Rivera: thanks all - recap in the notes and next steps in the chat. we'll follow up with links.

[45:00] (call ends)

Notes/links shared: Python quickstart repo (link), TypeScript quickstart repo (link), Benchmark script (link), Security FAQ (link), Console demo recording (link)
